chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Ayoub, from Abu Ubayda, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) judged regarding the man who had a wife in Basra, so he committed fornication in Kufa, that the stoning be deferred from him and the penalty of the fornicator be lashed.

He (peace be upon him) said: And he judged regarding a man imprisoned in prison, and for him was a free woman in his house in the city, and he could not reach her, so he committed adultery in the prison. He said: Upon him is the lashing, and the stoning is deferred from him.

key_terms.حَدَّ الزَّانِي: The fixed penalty for the fornicator/adulterer

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on stoning versus lashing for a married man who commits adultery in a different city or while imprisoned?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the juristic principle of 'tatabbu'' (marital availability) by illustrating two scenarios where Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) ruled that a man is exempt from stoning (rajm) and receives only lashing (jald). It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical accessibility of the spouse as a prerequisite for the 'muhsan' status, distinguishing between mere legal marriage and the practical ability to fulfill marital duties.
